final_candidates.decision_summary: Core RBM/ACE2-contact ridge position; conservative aromatic N->Y gain plausibly adds hydrophobic/π contacts with ACE2, with moderate plausibility (0.70). MSA non-support discounted given extremely shallow alignment (Neff 6).

RBM-adjacent surface position; Q->R adds positive charge complementary to acidic ACE2 surface, with near-neutral ESM-1v score (0.994) indicating minimal folding risk. No evolutionary support, so confidence stays moderate.

Only candidate with positive MSA support (K seen in homologs) plus decent plausibility (0.70); lysine on an exposed loop could favorably contact ACE2. Low coverage (3/8) and proximity to a disulfide context cap confidence.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence from all applicable tools is collected and further rounds would not alter the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Local 171 is Asn in the 'FQPTNGVGYQPYR' ACE2-contact motif, homologous to N501Y — the best-validated affinity-enhancing Spike mutation (Alpha and later variants). Tyrosine adds aromatic stacking with ACE2 Y41.
Corresponds to the well-documented N501Y substitution, which is experimentally known to increase ACE2 affinity via enhanced aromatic contact with ACE2 Y41; strong prior for the reward phenotype.

Retained as rank 1: this position lies in the core ACE2-contact ridge (RBM) where conservative aromatic gain (N->Y, mimicking affinity-enhancing aromatic substitutions) plausibly improves hydrophobic/π contacts with ACE2; plausibility (0.70) is moderate. MSA shows no homolog support, but Swiss-Prot depth is very shallow (Neff 6) so this is weak evidence against.
Ser at 147 corresponds to S477N, an affinity-enhancing mutation found in multiple variants that strengthens hydrogen bonding to ACE2 S19.
Corresponds to S477N, a repeatedly observed convergent variant associated with maintained/enhanced ACE2 binding near the interface.

Retained but demoted: plausibility is only moderate (0.67), no MSA support, and position sits next to a disulfide annotation context (148 region), raising local structural risk; S->N is a conservative change so kept in the pool as backup.
Gln at 168 corresponds to Q498R; paired with N501Y it formed the high-affinity Alpha RBD interface via a new salt bridge to ACE2 D38.
Corresponds to Q498R (Omicron-era change), which adds a favorable electrostatic contact to ACE2 D38 and is associated with increased affinity.

Reranked up to #2: near-neutral ESM-1v score (0.994) means structural/viability risk is minimal, and a Q->R charge gain on the RBM-adjacent surface could add electrostatic complementarity with acidic ACE2 surface residues. MSA non-support is from a very shallow alignment and is heavily discounted.
Thr at 148 corresponds to T478K (Delta-era mutation) reported to increase ACE2 binding and electrostatic complementarity at the interface.
Corresponds to T478K, a Delta-lineage mutation plausibly improving electrostatics with ACE2, though evidence is mixed.

Moved up to #3: only candidate besides N130K with positive MSA support (K seen in 1/3 homologs) plus decent plausibility (0.70); lysine gain on an exposed loop could favorably interact with ACE2. Coverage is low (3/8), so confidence stays moderate.
Asn at 130 corresponds to N460K, present in BA.2.75/BQ lineages and associated with improved ACE2 affinity.
Peripheral to the ACE2 contact patch; positive charge addition is speculative, kept as a lower-priority candidate.

Retained: best MSA support of the pool (K frequency 0.5, full 8/8 coverage), indicating strong evolutionary tolerance, but lowest plm score (0.60) and the position is further from the ACE2 interface, so capped below the top three.
Glu at 154 corresponds to E484K; affinity effects are context-dependent but charge reversal at this interface hotspot can enhance electrostatics with ACE2.
Corresponds to E484K, which affects interface electrostatics; affinity effect is context-dependent (known mainly for immune escape), so moderate confidence.
Retained: maximal plausibility (1.0) and charge reversal (E->K) could improve electrostatics toward acidic ACE2 patches, but zero MSA support and charge-swap risk keep it just outside the top three.
Gln at 163 corresponds to Q493R (Omicron), a direct ACE2-contact residue whose Arg substitution restores binding contacts.
Interface-adjacent residue where Arg could add polar contacts, but direct evidence is weak.
Retained: perfect plm score (1.0) and Q->R is a mild conservative charge addition on the RBM-adjacent surface; no evolutionary support, so confidence remains moderate.
Leu at 122 corresponds to L452R; primarily an immune-evasion mutation with mixed affinity effects, included as a lower-prior diversification candidate.
Position is far from the ACE2 binding interface; unlikely to affect the reward, downgraded pending evidence.

Rejected: despite plm score 1.0, the position is buried/β-strand with a nearby glycosylation site annotation and zero homolog support across 7 aligned sequences; L->R in a hydrophobic core-adjacent context is a folding risk with no clear ACE2-interface benefit.
